minutes.headline: Sewer Commission approved the Wright-Pierce contract and accepted counsel's changes to the Fitchburg sewer-use regulations.
minutes.summary: The commission reviewed the draft FY23 sewer budget, which carries last year's purchase-of-service amounts pending discussion with the DPW director. It voted on an engineering contract for the Upland Ave and White Street extension, and on counsel's recommended changes to two sections of the Fitchburg Chapter 147 regulations. It also discussed the maintenance contract rebid timing, ARPA guidance, policy changes for town meeting, and the assistant business manager search.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission passed counsel's recommended changes to sections 4-3 and 6-3 of the Fitchburg Chapter 147 sewer use regulations by roll call.
A vote on the Wright-Pierce contract for engineering design of the Upland Ave, White Street and Maple Parkway extension was recorded, but the outcome was not audible.
The draft FY23 sewer budget carries purchase of service at last year's amounts until the DPW director is consulted; the year-three maintenance contract increase is not included.
Staff will compile policy changes (easement, reconnection fee, grease trap, proration) for the next agenda, and the draft annual report goes on the February 8 agenda.

why_it_matters: The Fitchburg regulation changes govern how sewer users are treated, and the policy changes queued behind them, including the reconnection fee, could change what sewer customers are charged.
The FY23 sewer budget is still a draft with the maintenance contract increase left out, so the rates and spending residents see at town meeting may differ from this version.
watch_next: February 8 agenda: the draft annual report and the list of policy changes to coordinate with the Chapter 147 changes.
Confirmation of the Wright-Pierce contract vote outcome, which the recording does not make audible.
